My dear [Miss Butler](/person/237)
Thank you for your message. I do not think Rudolf requires to return to you for he stands so much alone that he only needs to be taken out.[^1]
Thanks too for the derivations, I shall trouble you with plenty more, I have no doubt, when I am at home with my list, and see my way out of the Latin derived names.[^2] I am to go home this afternoon after a very happy visit here. [Elizabeth Barnett](/person/113) is writing on the opposite side of the table, I wish I was going to take her back with me. My [mother](/person/1606) is reading your [philosophe](/topic/154) with great delight

yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: CMY had asked Butler to delete a passage from her series of articles [Aunt Louisa\'s Travels](/organisation/242).
[^2]: CMY had asked Butler\'s help with Scandinavian names for the series of articles in [MP](/periodical/52) called \'Name-Fancying\' which later became [A History of Christian Names](/book/48).
